'''Jerdarrian "JD" Davison''' (born October 3, 2002) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top [[point guard]]s in the 2021 class.

==High school career==
Davison attended Calhoun High School in [[Letohatchee, Alabama]].<ref name="long">{{cite web |last1=Long |first1=A. Stacy |title=Oh, brother: J.D. follows well-worn Davison path as Calhoun star |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/2019/04/01/oh-brother-j-d-follows-well-worn-davison-path-calhoun-tigers-all-metro-star/3324825002/ |website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]] |access-date=April 17, 2021 |date=April 1, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Toran |first1=Andre |title=God may have 'forgot' Lowndes County, but he blessed it with 4-star point guard JD Davison |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/2020/02/03/god-may-have-forgot-lowndes-county-but-he-blessed-4-star-pg-jd-davison/4540582002/ |website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]] |access-date=April 17, 2021 |date=February 3, 2020}}</ref> As a junior, Davison averaged 30.4 points, 12 rebounds and five assists per game, earning [[Alabama Mr. Basketball]] and Alabama [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] honors.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Thomas |first1=Ben |title=Calhoun junior guard J.D. Davison named Alabama's Mr. Basketball for 2020 |url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/2020/04/calhoun-junior-guard-jd-davison-named-alabamas-mr-basketball-for-2020.html |website=AL.com |access-date=April 17, 2021 |date=April 4, 2020}}</ref> He led his team to a Class 2A state title, converting a game-winning three-pointer as part of a 34-point, 10-rebound performance in the title game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Thomas |first1=Ben |title=J.D. Davison's buzzer-beater wins Class 2A boys title for Calhoun |url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/2020/02/jd-davisons-buzzer-beater-wins-class-2a-boys-title-for-calhoun.html |website=AL.com |access-date=April 17, 2021 |date=February 28, 2020}}</ref> As a senior, Davison averaged 32.4 points, 10.9 rebounds and 4.7 assists per game. He was selected as Alabama Mr. Basketball for a second consecutive season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sutton |first1=Hailey |title=JD Davison named Mr. Basketball 2021 |url=https://www.wsfa.com/2021/04/12/jd-davison-named-mr-basketball/ |website=[[WSFA]] |access-date=April 18, 2021 |date=April 11, 2021}}</ref> Davison was named to the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]] rosters.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Blackwell |first1=Joey |title=Alabama Basketball Signee J.D. Davison Named McDonald's All-American |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/alabama-signee-j-d-davison-named-mcdonalds-all-american-blackwell |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=April 18, 2021 |date=February 23, 2021}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Davison was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top [[point guard]]s in the 2021 class. On October 3, 2020, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] over offers from [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]]. He became the first five-star recruit during the tenure of head coach [[Nate Oats]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Five-star recruit J.D. Davison, ESPN's No. 2 point guard, picks Alabama Crimson Tide |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30032393/five-star-recruit-jd-davison-espn-no-2-point-guard-picks-alabama-crimson-tide |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=April 17, 2021 |date=October 3, 2020}}</ref> He was drawn to Alabama in part because he wanted to remain close to home.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gunter |first1=Stephen |title=Calhoun basketball star JD Davison is Bama bound |url=https://www.wsfa.com/2020/11/14/calhoun-basketball-star-jd-davison-is-bama-bound/ |website=[[WSFA]] |access-date=April 17, 2021 |date=November 14, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman, Davison averaged 8.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 4.3 assists per game.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kelly |first1=Nick |title=Alabama basketball guard JD Davison's hair: He's been working on it since second grade |url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2022/03/18/jd-davison-hair-alabama-ncaa-tournament-2022-march-madness/7083893001/ |access-date=March 22, 2022 |work=[[The Tuscaloosa News]] |date=March 18, 2022}}</ref> He was named to the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team.<ref name=SECAwardsC>{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/33453309/men-basketball-all-sec-teams-awards-announced|title=Men's Basketball All-SEC Teams & Awards Announced |publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}}</ref> On April 13, 2022, Davison declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alabama Crimson Tide freshman guard JD Davison to enter NBA draft|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33734282/alabama-crimson-tide-freshman-guard-jd-davison-enter-nba-draft|date=April 13, 2022|accessdate=April 14, 2022}}</ref>
